questions.question: What is your biggest challenge?
questions.answer:
The hardest thing I've built was the Go microservices settlement layer for a crypto exchange — it had to handle real money with zero tolerance for error.

**Money = zero tolerance.** Every transaction is a financial contract. A single miscalculation means real loss. I designed atomic transactions, idempotent APIs, and reconciliation pipelines to ensure no double-spend and no discrepancies.

**Distributed systems complexity.** Coordinating wallet, ledger, and KYC across services while maintaining eventual consistency required the saga pattern, message queues, and designing for failure at every hop.

**Concurrency & race conditions.** Preventing balance corruption under simultaneous top-up, transfer, and withdrawal requests demanded optimistic locking plus Redis-based distributed locks on critical paths.

**KYC & compliance.** Integrating AWS Rekognition for face-match identity verification while maintaining audit trails for every cent moved — in a regulated environment.

**What I learned:** Correctness beats features every time. Build defensively, instrument for observability, and treat every transaction as a contract. That mindset now applies to everything I build.
